Phase 0.summary: GDN expanded-K blocked conclusion is fixed. ek4-ev4 smoke forward/backward passed; ek8-ev2 is blocked by FLA chunk state-update K<=256 assertion; ek16-ev1 was not launched because it requires per-head K=1024 under the same limit.
Phase 0.ledger_policy: Smoke, blocked, failed, and not-launched rows are not official training results and were not written to canonical ledger.

Phase 1.summary: Kernel-compatible GDN Phase 1 completed: ek4-ev4, mh-h4-k256-v128, and mh-h8-k256-v64 all finished 4epoch seed123 training with GDN_KERNEL_DTYPE=float32. mh-h4-k256-v128 is best among the three by final overall accuracy and 1024x256 hard accuracy.
Phase 1.next_step: Re-read plan, then enter Phase 2 to run Flash-VQG cb256-r8-s126 and cb256-r16-s126 stability seeds.
Phase 1.notes: First formal launch attempt exited before training because PARALLELIZE=true/-p required ray, which is not installed. Runner now defaults PARALLELIZE=false so sequential launch does not require ray. The failed launch has planned runs only and was not written to official ledger.

Phase 2.summary: Phase 2 Flash-VQG stability check completed. New b64_ga4 fp32 official runs were completed for cb256-r8-s126 and cb256-r6-s125; existing b64_ga4 fp32 results were reused for cb256-r16-s126 and cb256-r10-s125. Results show Flash rank/seed behavior is non-monotonic: r10-s125 is currently strongest, r6-s125 is competitive on hard slice, r8-s126 is weak, and r16-s126 is below r10.
Phase 2.comparison_note: Compared with Phase 1 best GDN mh-h4-k256-v128, Flash r10-s125 is stronger but has larger active_state_capacity. Same active capacity comparison remains close between best GDN and cb64-r16 seed123; Phase 2 primarily evaluates Flash mainline stability rather than same-capacity fairness.

Phase 3.trigger_review: Phase 1 mh-h4/mh-h8 improved over ek4 and did not falsify address-capacity route; training cost was acceptable, so Banked-K GDN is implemented for Phase 3.
Phase 3.summary: Phase 3 Banked-K GDN shared-V completed. It keeps logical_heads=2 with 4 banks per head and per-kernel K=256,V=64, reaches valid_accuracy=0.9973046875 and hard 1024x256=0.9799609375 at seed123, outperforming Phase 1 mh-h4-k256-v128 on both overall and hard slice while keeping active_state_capacity=131072.
Phase 3.next_step: Re-read plan, then enter Phase 4 to add multi-seed only for winning points. Banked-K qualifies because seed123 is clearly promising.

active_run.note: Formal cloud SwanLab run. Earlier disabled-mode launch 2026-05-26T18:56:41Z was debug-only and terminated during epoch 0.

debug_launch_attempt.reason: Started with SWANLAB_MODE=disabled only to confirm launch path; terminated during epoch 0 and not official.

Phase 4.trigger_review: Banked-K seed123 is clearly promising: valid_accuracy 0.9973046875 and hard 1024x256 0.9799609375, better than Phase 1 best GDN mh-h4-k256-v128. Proceed to selective multi-seed planning/execution per Phase 4, not broad grid expansion.
Phase 4.summary: Selective multi-seed Phase 4 completed for Banked-K GDN seeds 124, 125, and 126, combined with Phase 3 seed123. Banked-K seed123/126 are stronger than Phase 1 increased-head GDN seed123, but the 4-seed mean is lower than mh-h4 seed123 on both overall and hard accuracy because seed124/125 drop substantially. It should be reported as high-upside but seed-sensitive, not as a stable win over increased-head GDN yet.
Phase 4.next_step: Re-read plan before Phase 5. Because Banked-K is promising but seed-sensitive, Phase 5 should be treated as OOD/generic retrieval validation only after comparing against the selected Flash multiseed anchors.

Phase 5.summary: Phase 5 longer-MQAR OOD completed for mh-h4 seed123 and Banked-K seeds 123-126. All 25 formal eval rows completed with dataset_hash consistent by slice. Banked-K seed123/126 outperform mh-h4 seed123 on most OOD slices, but the four-seed Banked-K mean is lower than mh-h4 seed123 on all five slices because seeds 124/125 degrade substantially. This confirms the Phase 4 high-upside but seed-sensitive conclusion under OOD evaluation.

verification.timing_fields_present: started_at_utc, ended_at_utc, wall_clock_sec, gpu, gpu_name, status are present in phase5 detail/status CSV after deterministic backfill for historical rows.
verification.timing_backfill_method: For rows generated before native timing wrapper support, started_at_utc is created_at_utc - wall_clock_sec and ended_at_utc is created_at_utc. Future Phase 5 wrapper runs write native timing fields.

Phase 5.not_run_reason: The minimum Phase 5 stopping criterion was longer-MQAR OOD. Results are already decisive enough to support Phase 6 gate decision; passkey/needle and LM slice should be separate follow-up tasks if needed.

Phase 6.summary: Phase 6 gate is triggered. Kernel-compatible GDN variants do not remove the fairness concern: Banked-K has high single-seed upside but poor multi-seed stability, and existing same-capacity Flash cb64-r16 seed123 is much stronger on longer-MQAR OOD than Banked-K multi-seed mean and mh-h4 seed123. Therefore true per-head K=1024,V=64 GDN remains the cleanest endpoint if the paper needs to isolate address/key capacity. This should be started as an independent FLA kernel research goal, not mixed into the current experiment run.
go_conditions_met: Banked-K result is insufficient to remove fairness concern because multi-seed mean is below mh-h4 seed123 and far below same-capacity Flash cb64-r16 on longer-MQAR OOD.
Flash remains clearly stronger than kernel-compatible GDN on longer-MQAR OOD, especially 2048x512 and longer slices.
A true K=1024,V=64 GDN baseline is still missing because FLA chunk state-update kernel blocks per-head K>256.
Phase 6.next_independent_goal: Implement or evaluate a fork of fla-org/flash-linear-attention with K-blocked Gated Delta Rule chunk state-update kernel supporting per-head K=512,V=128 and K=1024,V=64, using naive_recurrent_gated_delta_rule as correctness oracle and preserving K<=256 old path behavior.
